x: This was held at Wimbledon on October 24th jointly with a match against Herne Hill H. and Sutton and Cheam Harriers. Maynard, Clark and Heywood were the first three home, followed by Chas, Walker and P.
Heywood scored a runaway victory from Barrett of Ealing with Eldon taking third place inside Stan Cox's record of 54.19. Dave Baulch finished 4th, 9 secs outside the previous record.

10 miles in 51m.48secs. by Jack Heywood with Colin then fifth in 58m.6secs. and Wally in 61m.4secs. was to lead to a new English Amateur Native Record for 15 miles in 1hr.17m.25secs. by Heywood who then retired.

Albans' O'Gorman,at that time well behind us.Jack gave Heywood of H.H.H a fright and was unlucky not to catch him before Handcross. The traffic here was exceptionally thick and a slight contretemps with a large car might well have proved serious to our runners.
Jack's progress was a treat to watch, for from 6 miles he slowly went through to pass Keily, Hicks, Heywood, our second claim member Bill Bird, running a 'blinder', and was soon lying about 15th.

Once again Jack established a new lap record, but failed to catch Heywood of H.H.H. who also put up a very fast time. The 5th stage run by Jumbo Masters, saw us drop to 3rd place behind T.V.H. and H.H.H. and our last man, Eric Gebbett, although running well was unable to improve on this.
